# P35.55 — Rollback, withdrawal, purge, runbook, legacy floor (REL-08)

**Ticket:**
`docs/tickets/333_P35.55__rollback-withdrawal-purge-runbook.md`
(manifest row **333**, Round 11 / P35). Invoked `live_verification=false`
— no gate, not OM-20; leg runs: 0. Everything hosted stays deferred:
the roll legs are engineered and composed-proven with injected runners,
`--execute-rolls` remains the operator's switch, and no production or
staging mutation happens in this row. Owned: **REL-08** (rollback,
clear-latest, withdrawal, legacy-floor import, and the purge posture).
Served: **SIG-REL-013** (the withdrawal barrier is append-only and a
rollback never resurrects withdrawn material), **SIG-OPS-004** (the

**GT-3** (no live rollback to a stale revision), **GT-9** (the barrier

hashed-archive postures preserved). **Base:**
`r11/P35.54-config-generations-metadata-only-promotion` (PR #352).
**Gate:** none. **Closes:** `D-P35.54-1` — verify→promote withdrawal
drift is now re-derived under the promote lock.

## What landed

- **`ops/src/ops/release_reversal.py`** — the five operator-commanded
  verbs plus their shared machinery, all dry-run by default and all
  fail-closed:

  - **`sig-ops release rollback --to <pub|label|legacy-floor> --reason
    <why> --go <authority>`** — resolves the target against
    `promoted.map`, labels, and `registry/floor.json`; refuses a roll
    to the current pointer (a no-op would still mint a generation),
    to a never-promoted namespace, or to a pub under a current denying
    release-level disposition (the landed `exports.rollback` refusal,
    wrapped). It **re-derives the current withdrawal barrier** before
    composing `conf/<gen+1>` — a rollback re-points the latest view,
    it never un-denies. The roll plan is `sig-api` then `sig-web`
    **new-revision** orders (`SIG_CONF_GEN`/`SIG_LATEST_PUB` env pairs);
    Cloud Run `update-traffic`/`--to-revisions` is never issued because
    an old revision's pinned generation could re-serve withdrawn routes
    (GT-3). Journals `rolled-back` and `rolled-back-from`.
  - **`sig-ops release clear-latest --reason <why> --go <authority>`**
    — the archive-only emergency posture: writes a generation whose
    latest pointer carries `SIG_LATEST_PUB=none` /
    `no-current-release`, so `/` 404s honestly under `v/none/` while
    every promoted namespace, `/releases/`, and the withdrawal barrier
    keep serving. The env pair stays fully set — the entrypoint's
    half-set guard never trips. Journals `cleared-latest`.
  - **`sig-ops release withdraw --disposition
    <sig.withdrawal-order/1> --authority <sig.operator-authority/1>`**
    — validates the order, verifies the authority record exists,
    unexpired and unrevoked (a missing/malformed/expired record refuses
    — authority is never fabricated), then appends
    `sig.disposition/1` records via the landed `record_withdrawal`
    (append-only; never an edit). `apply_withdrawals` walks **every
    staged namespace** (`r/`, `s/`, `v/`, `releases/`, site stubs) so
    the deny reaches every serving alias: no-slash, trailing-slash,
    `index.html`, and the `.json` twin each get a `location =` line in
    `withdrawn.conf` plus a dated, public-safe `sig.tombstone/1` body
    under `staged/conf/tombstone/`. Writes `conf/<gen+1>` (latest
    pointer stamped `withdrawals_sha256`), plans the api→web
    new-revision roll, fires the dormant mirror/cache `purge_hooks`
    (recorded no-op without a configured mirror), optionally runs
    `--purge-versions` (noncurrent object-generation purge, below),
    then probes every denied alias — optionally requiring origin HTTP
    410 — and records a `sig.withdrawal-receipt/1` under
    `registry/receipts/` carrying `claim_spine_touched: false`.
  - **`sig-ops release import-floor --from <dir> --as
    legacy-YYYYMMDD`** — stages the tree under
    `staged/v/legacy-<date>/`, writes `registry/floor.json`
    (`sig.legacy-floor/1`), journals `legacy-floor-imported`. A
    `p-`-shaped name refuses: a floor is a label, never a publication
    id.
  - **`sig-ops release conf-gen-probe --origin <url>`** — the P1
    regression probe: reads the recorded generation, measures each
    origin's `X-SIG-Conf-Gen`, journals `sig.probe-run/1`.
    served-older → rollback-revival alarm; served-newer/unrecorded →
    fail. Measured, never asserted.
  - **Shared machinery** — `registry_view`/`sync_registry_back`/
    `sync_staged_back` bridge the bucket layout (`registry/*` +
    `staged/*`) into the `exports.release` registry model through a
    scratch view (symlinked `staged/` on `LocalDirStore`, a mirrored
    tree + metageneration-matched write-back on `GcsStore`), so the
    landed `record_withdrawal`/`apply_withdrawals`/`rollback`/
    `clear_latest_pointer` run verbatim. `compose_reversal_generation`
    carries the immutable generation pieces and replaces only the
    latest pointer + deny-map outputs.
- **Compartment-scoped dispositions** — `policy.DispositionRecord`
  gains an optional `compartment` field (additive; absent records are
  unchanged); `exports.release` serializes it round-trip and
  `apply_withdrawals` + the route-binding paths honour it, so an order
  scoped to `sig_graph` denies only routes under `c/sig_graph/` —
  the deny never crosses a licence compartment boundary.
- **Promote-time withdrawal drift — `D-P35.54-1` closed** —
  `latest.json` now stamps `withdrawals_sha256` and `verb_promote`
  compares the prior generation's recorded digest against the live
  registry digest at lock time; on drift it re-derives `withdrawn.conf`
  from the current withdrawal state (the `derive_withdrawal_barrier`
  hook, invoked not re-implemented) before composing. A second in-lock
  digest read refuses if the registry shifts inside the derive/write
  seam.
- **GCS version purge** — `GcsBucket.list_object_versions(prefix)` +
  generation-qualified `delete_object` back `--purge-versions`: only
  **noncurrent** object generations of objects a withdrawal
  removed/tombstoned are deleted (bucket bytes only, for legal
  takedowns). The live generation is always excluded; the claim spine
  has no delete path and gained none.
- **CLI + dispatch** — `release_pipeline.run_verb` dispatches all five
  verbs (`VERB_OWNERS` no longer defers them) and wires `verb_promote`
  to the derive hook; `cli.py` gains the full option surface with the
  common registry/apply/lock arguments.
- **`docs/ops/RUNBOOK.md`** — three appended sections (republish,
  rollback + clear-latest, withdrawal/takedown) covering the
  dry-run-first discipline, operator authority, new-revision rolls,
  alias probes, tombstones, mirror purge hooks, `--purge-versions`, and
  the receipt/audit expectations. `check_runbook.py`: 9/9 sections,
  55 command lines, 0 violations.

## What did not land (owned elsewhere)

- The V1–V14 verification suite and post-promote auto-rollback —
  P35.56/P35.58 (the conf-gen probe lands here; the suite wires it).
- Any hosted apply leg — `D-P35.53-1` (OP-24) and `D-R10-PUBLISH-1`
  stand; nothing public was touched.
- Mirror/cache purge beyond the wired hooks — mirrors stay
  configuration-driven; without one the hook is a recorded no-op.
- Live `--purge-versions` execution — exercised only against fixture
  stores.

## Notes for reviewers

- The exports/ops layout bridge is the one seam to read carefully:
  `registry_view` gives `exports.release` the tree shape it expects,
  and `sync_*_back` writes changes through generation preconditions —
  on `GcsStore` a metageneration drift fails the write-back closed.
- `clear-latest` uses the literal pub sentinel `none`: `v/none/` is
  guaranteed absent by construction, so the latest view 404s without a
  single special-case location in nginx.
- The probe distinguishes "older than recorded" (the rollback-revival
  alarm) from "newer/unrecorded" (a different failure class) — both
  fail, but the record names which.
